prerequisites: The student masters the elementary concepts of strength of materials and can apply them in simple concrete situations.
Torsion, principal stresses, principal strains, max. shear stresses

learning_outcomes.text: After successful completion of this course, the student understands the concept of representative volume elements and can apply it to describe the mechanical behavior of biological tissues, including bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, ligaments, tendons, blood vessels, and brain, at different length scales.
The student can relate the mechanical properties of biological tissues to the geometry and internal structure of these tissues.
The student can formulate and interpret relevant constitutive equations, including linear-elastic, viscoelastic, hyperelastic, and biphasic material behavior, for biological tissues.
The student can estimate mechanical consequences of pathologies and degenerative diseases.

The student has knowledge of experimental testing techniques, including uniaxial and biaxial tensile tests, confined and unconfined compression tests, three- and four-point bending, to quantify mechanical properties of biological tissues.
The student is able to obtain material parameters of constitutive equations from experimental tests.

syllabus_topics: Mechanical description at different length scales of biological tissues, including bone, cartilage, intervertebral discs, ligaments, tendons, blood vessels, and brain
Constitutive equations including linear-elastic, viscoelastic, hyperelastic, and biphasic material behavior

Experimental testing techniques, including uniaxial and biaxial tensile tests, confined and unconfined compression tests, three- and four-point bending, to quantify mechanical properties of biological tissues
Introduction to experimental tests; determination of material parameters of constitutive equations.
institution: KU Leuven - Faculty of Engineering Science
degree: Bachelor in de ingenieurswetenschappen (Bachelor of Engineering Science, Leuven)
